notes.title: How the food list works
notes.body: Youngstown's signature is Brier Hill pizza — a pepper-and-romano pie with little or no mozzarella. A cuisine tag needs a named dish, not a label. Anything tagged ADDED is from general knowledge and should be verified before a visit.

localFavourites.rule: Open places recommended only by local press, local writers or vetted creators — none by an official or tourism source, and every source typed in our registry.

places.w: Opened in 1919 as the first museum in the country built solely for American art, with more than 20,000 works from Winslow Homer to the present. Free, and the anchor of the Wick Avenue museum row — the piece of Youngstown that draws visitors from out of state.
places.k: Free. Open Tuesday–Sunday. Approximate map pin.

places.n: Youngstown Historical Center of Industry and Labor
places.w: The Steel Museum — an Ohio History Connection site that tells the rise and collapse of the mills that built Youngstown, straight and unsentimental. The essential stop for understanding what this city was and what happened to it.
places.k: Admission charged. Check open days; often Wed–Sat.

places.w: YSU's history-of-medicine museum: office recreations, nursing and x-ray exhibits, and a bright yellow 1952 Emerson iron lung as its centrepiece. Founded 1985; now in Cushwa Hall. An Atlas Obscura listing.
places.k: Free. Campus building — check hours; parking is easier on weekends.

places.ad: Ward Beecher Science Hall, 100 Lincoln Ave
places.w: A well-regarded university planetarium that has run free public shows since 1967 — typically Friday and Saturday evenings and Saturday afternoons, September through May.
places.k: Free, no reservations. Doors 30 min early; latecomers cannot enter once dark. Shows Sept–May.

places.w: A 1905 Arts-and-Crafts mansion run by the Mahoning Valley Historical Society, furnished as it was and used to tell the story of the Valley's industrial families.
places.k: Admission charged. Closed Mondays; check seasonal hours.

places.w: A 1926 neoclassical concert hall with a marble-columned front, one of the finest rooms in the region and still a working venue, just north of Wick Park.
places.k: Ticketed events; the exterior is worth a look any time.

places.w: Youngstown State's contemporary art museum, directly across Wick Avenue from the Butler. Rotating shows of new and student work. Free.
places.k: Free. Often closed between exhibitions — check the current show.

places.w: A quiet hidden gem for rock hounds inside YSU — fluorescent minerals, fossils and crystals, free to walk through. Small, specific, and exactly the kind of thing this guide is for.
places.k: Free. Campus building; limited hours — check before going.

places.ad: Fifth Ave & Park Ave, North Side
places.w: A 34-acre 19th-century park ringed by the North Side's grand old mansions. A stroll and some architecture, not a ticket.
places.k: Free, daylight hours. Nicer by day.

places.w: An 1845–46 grist mill, restored and still grinding corn, wheat and buckwheat with the creek's rushing water, beside a waterfall. The picture-book heart of Mill Creek Park.
places.k: Seasonal — roughly May through October. Small admission. Approximate pin.

places.w: Free formal gardens overlooking Lake Glacier, with the Davis visitor center, a cafe and long seasonal colour. Part of Mill Creek MetroParks and one of the loveliest free things in the Valley.
places.k: Free. Gardens open daily; Davis Center has its own hours.

places.n: Mill Creek Suspension Bridge (the Cinderella Bridge)
places.w: The slender 86-foot pedestrian suspension span locals call the Cinderella Bridge, recently restored to its arches-and-spires opulence. The park's signature photo, and an Atlas Obscura listing.
places.k: Free, always open. Approximate pin — it sits on a park trail.

places.w: A restored pond circled by the quarter-mile Lily Pond Circle Trail — a short, flat, genuinely peaceful loop, revived from years of neglect with bioswales and permeable paving.
places.k: Free. Easy quarter-mile loop; good with kids. Approximate pin.

places.w: At 60 acres the largest of the park's three lakes. Kayaks and pedal boats rent from the Newport Boathouse in season — the easiest way to get out on the water in the city.
places.k: Boat rentals seasonal; the drive around the lakes is open year-round.

places.ad: Fellows Riverside Gardens, Mill Creek Park
places.w: A formal rose garden within Fellows Riverside Gardens, growing many classes of roses — at its best in June and July.
places.k: Free, within the gardens. Peak bloom early summer.

places.ad: 840 Old Furnace Rd, Mill Creek Park
places.w: A stone-house nature center and trailhead into the wooded interior of Mill Creek Park, with exhibits and easy walks.
places.k: Free. Check hours; trails open dawn to dusk.

places.w: An 1821 stone woolen-mill building, one of the oldest structures around, remodeled in 1893 and now a rentable pavilion for reunions and receptions.
places.k: Free to look; rentable for events. Combine with Lanterman's Mill.

places.ad: 1 W Golf Dr, Mill Creek Park
places.w: Two 18-hole, par-70 championship courses that opened to the public in 1928, laid through the park's woods — a genuine draw for golfers.
places.k: Tee times through the MetroParks. Seasonal. Approximate pin.

places.w: Home of the Youngstown Symphony, behind a 1931 movie-palace facade on West Federal Street. The Valley's main stage for orchestra, ballet and touring shows.
places.k: Ticketed performances. Lobby worth a peek on show nights.

places.w: The Historical Society's downtown museum of Mahoning Valley history, in a restored former department store on West Federal Street.
places.k: Admission charged. Check open days before going.

places.n: Roger & Gloria Jones Children's Center for Science & Technology
places.w: A hands-on STEM center for kids that opened in 2011, with interactive science and technology exhibits — the family stop downtown.
places.k: Admission charged; best for children. Check hours. Approximate pin.

places.w: Among the oldest continuously operating community theaters in the United States, staging affordable productions on the South Side.
places.k: Tickets are cheap; check the season's schedule.

places.w: The downtown riverfront arena — Phantoms hockey, concerts and events, and the anchor of the eastern edge of downtown.
places.k: Event venue; nothing to see when dark. Check the calendar.

places.ad: around W Federal St & Central Square
places.w: A growing set of large downtown murals, several honoured statewide, that have brightened the old commercial core. Walkable in an afternoon between Central Square and the arts district.
places.k: Free, outdoors, always up. Ask at a downtown shop for the current mural map. Approximate pin.

places.w: A 1910 Renaissance Revival landmark by Charles F. Owsley whose interior opens into a roughly 100-foot rotunda crowned by a glazed art-glass dome, ringed by marble columns, mahogany and courtroom murals.
places.k: Working courthouse; the interior is best seen on the periodic free public tours. Security screening applies. Approximate pin.

places.w: A brick alley in downtown Warren painted wall-to-wall in tribute to Warren-born Nirvana/Foo Fighters drummer Dave Grohl — murals, a metal figure at a drum kit, and a pair of 900-pound drumsticks billed as the world's largest.
places.k: Free, outdoors. In Warren, about 20 minutes north; pair with a Modern Methods beer next door.

places.w: A columned memorial and museum to President William McKinley in his birthplace of Niles, a short drive north of Youngstown. Free, and grander than you expect for a small city.
places.k: Free. In Niles, about 15 minutes away. Check museum hours.

places.w: Home of the Canfield Fair, Ohio's largest county fair, over Labor Day week. The grounds are quiet off-season.
places.k: The fair is late Aug–Labor Day. Otherwise little to see. Seasonal.

places.w: The beloved Idora Park amusement park closed in 1984; volunteers now keep a museum of its memorabilia. A piece of vanished Youngstown, opened only on select days.
places.k: Limited hours — call or check ahead. The park itself is long gone. Approximate pin.

places.w: A retro pinball-and-arcade museum in a former Girard supermarket holding roughly 600 largely playable pinball machines plus 200+ classic arcade games from the 1930s on — one of the largest such collections in the country, assembled by Pinball Expo founder Rob Berk.
places.k: Opened 2023. Thu–Fri from 4pm, Sat–Sun from 11am; ~$20 adults / $10 ages 6–16 for unlimited play; allow 3+ hours. ~10 min north, off I-80. Approximate pin.

places.w: A 23,000-sq-ft museum on the site where the Packard automobile was born in 1899 — rotating original and restored Packards, classic motorcycles, and the Packard family and company archives.
places.k: Tue–Sat 12–5, Sun 1–5; closed Mondays and holidays. In Warren, ~20 min north. Approximate pin.

places.w: A meticulously restored 1923 Art Deco/Mediterranean theatre by C. Howard Crane — a 1,400-seat house that reopened in 2020, ninety-seven years to the day after its debut, and now books national touring music and comedy.
places.k: Ticketed events; check the schedule. In downtown Warren, ~20 min north. Approximate pin.

places.n: Noah's Lost Ark Exotic Animal Sanctuary
places.w: A nonprofit no-kill exotic-animal sanctuary — lions, tigers, bears and 125+ rescued animals — one of the few facilities both state- and federally licensed to give guided public tours.
places.k: Seasonal, roughly May 15–Oct 31; petting zoo, gift shop, free noon tortoise feeding. ~30 min west. Approximate pin.

places.w: A free classic-car museum inside the TP Tools complex — 50+ restored autos from 1917 on, staged amid immersive period sets: a 1950s diner, soda bar, country store and service garage.
places.k: Free; typically Saturdays 10–3, hours limited — confirm ahead. ~20 min south. Approximate pin.

places.w: A 402-acre working farm run by Mill Creek MetroParks — animal barns, the interactive AgVenture Barn, a free fall corn maze, disc golf and a natural playground — and the trailhead for the 11-mile MetroParks Bikeway.
places.k: Seasonal, roughly April–October; free admission. Pumpkin harvest and Bug Day in season. ~20 min south. Approximate pin.

places.w: A long-running outdoor family fun center in Boardman — go-kart tracks, 18-hole adventure golf, batting cages and a redemption arcade — the valley's go-to for arcade-plus-outdoor play.
places.k: Seasonal outdoor attractions; pay-per-ride or packages. ~15 min south. Approximate pin.

places.n: Hollywood Gaming at Mahoning Valley Race Course
places.w: A racino (2014) pairing a one-mile thoroughbred track with 1,100+ video lottery terminals, dining and events — the region's live horse-racing venue.
places.k: Gaming areas 21+; live thoroughbred racing roughly Oct–April, free to watch. ~15 min northwest. Approximate pin.

places.ad: 4033 North River Rd NE, Warren, OH
places.w: A small but rich aviation museum honouring pioneer Ernest C. Hall — his 1947 Piper PA-12, personal letters between Hall and Orville Wright, and a scrap of fabric from the Red Baron's Fokker triplane.
places.k: Nonprofit, limited hours; hosts Wings-n-Wheels fly-ins. Confirm hours first. ~25 min north. Approximate pin.

places.w: An 1862 fourteen-room Victorian mansion on the National Register, home to the Niles Historical Society's 5,000+ artefacts of local industrial heritage and reproductions of several First Ladies' inaugural gowns.
places.k: Very limited hours — typically the first Sunday of the month, 2–5, or by appointment. ~15 min north. Approximate pin.

places.w: An 1831 covered bridge over the Mahoning River — the oldest covered bridge still in service in Ohio, with a rare attached covered pedestrian walkway.
places.k: Free, open to traffic and on foot year-round. ~25 min northwest. Approximate pin.

places.w: Open since 1927. The dish is a Brier Hill 'Smoky Hollow' pizza — tomato, bell peppers and grated romano — eaten beside the bocce courts out back. As Youngstown as it gets.
places.k: Italian institution; bocce in season. Confirm hours.

places.w: A downtown Italian spot that regularly tops the city's restaurant lists, praised for its ricotta board and made-to-order pastas.
places.k: Popular; reservations help on weekends. Approximate pin.

places.w: A classic Jewish delicatessen north of downtown, widely called the best corned beef in the Valley — plus rye, latkes and the rest of the deli canon.
places.k: Lunch counter; go for the corned beef. Approximate pin.

places.w: Founded here in the summer of 1945 by Alice Handel at her husband's gas station; the original South Side stand still scoops. Now 175+ stores nationwide, with its HQ in Canfield.
places.k: Cash-friendly, seasonal lines. The original location marks Handel's roots.

places.w: A 1932 Brier Hill Italian-American landmark on Logan Avenue. It closed in 2017 and has since reopened — running again, tied to the neighbourhood's pizza lore.
places.k: Reopened after 2017; confirm current hours before going.

places.w: A local pizzeria since 1967 that makes the classic Brier Hill pie — tomato, bell peppers and grated romano, with little or no mozzarella.
places.k: In Austintown, west of the city. Ask for the Brier Hill pie by name.

places.w: A brick-walled downtown spot serving Brier Hill pizza alongside inventions like a Pesto Hot Honey pie.
places.k: Downtown; good lunch stop between museums.

places.w: A bar and gathering spot on Federal Plaza with a patio and frequent live music — the social heart of downtown after dark, with a solid American menu.
places.k: Bar/venue; check the music calendar. Approximate pin.

places.w: A long-running cafe known for towering cakes, pastries and coffee, with a comfortable downtown room for a slower stop.
places.k: Cafe hours; save room for cake. Approximate pin.

places.w: A downtown microbrewery in a historic church, all beer made onsite, specialising in wild ales and lagers — a distinctive taproom.
places.k: Taproom hours vary; check before you go. Approximate pin.

places.w: A downtown brewery in a former warehouse, pitched as Youngstown's go-to hometown beer, with a big room, a disco ball and live music. Named for the city's old 'Penguin' nickname.
places.k: Taproom; check hours and events. Approximate pin.

places.n: St. Anthony of Padua parish pizza
places.w: The Brier Hill church that sells hundreds of pizzas a week as a parish fundraiser — takeout, cash, and a genuine piece of neighbourhood lore.
places.k: Fundraiser hours only — call ahead. Cash. Approximate pin.

places.w: A well-liked Italian restaurant that turns up alongside the city's best, for a sit-down red-sauce dinner.
places.k: Dinner; confirm hours. Approximate pin.

places.w: Warren's first craft brewery since 1880, opened 2018 right on Dave Grohl Alley — IPAs, stouts and pilsners in a mural-wrapped tasting room.
places.k: In Warren, ~20 min north; pair with Dave Grohl Alley.

places.w: A community-minded small brewery in nearby Columbiana with a dozen rotating craft beers on tap — worth the drive south.
places.k: In Columbiana, ~25 min south. Check taproom hours. Approximate pin.

places.w: A permanent indoor Amish market on South Avenue: bulk foods, baked goods, produce, meats, cheese and dairy, plus Amish furniture and a hot-food restaurant, all under one roof. A genuine fixture, not a pop-up.
places.k: Thu 9–6, Fri 9–6, Sat 8–4; closed Sun–Wed. Cash-friendly. Approximate pin.

places.w: Youngstown's oldest farmers market, running since 2003 near Wick Park — a dozen-plus local growers with produce, preserves, plants and prepared food, and the occasional live music or demo. Small but excellent, and a genuine community institution.
places.k: Saturday mornings (about 10–1); seasonal, so check the schedule before going. Publicly open.

places.w: Downtown's premier 'Market for Makers' — a monthly, tightly curated indoor/outdoor market of local artists, vintage sellers, antique and repurposed furniture, apparel and food that draws treasure-hunters from across the region. One of the best reasons to be downtown on a market day.
places.k: Monthly during its season — check youngstownflea.com for dates before going. Publicly open.

places.w: The largest open-air flea market in the tri-state area — over five miles of aisles and 1,000-plus vendor spaces of antiques, vintage, tools, produce and famous Amish doughnuts, going strong year-round. A proper day out for treasure hunters.
places.k: Fridays only, 7:30am to mid-afternoon, year-round. About 35–40 min south; wear walking shoes.

places.w: A big Canfield orchard and farm market open weekdays and weekends: orchard-fresh and pick-your-own apples, seasonal produce, and a fall gift barn famous for its apple-cider doughnuts and cider. The Valley's autumn tradition.
places.k: Open much of the year; busiest in fall. About 20 min out. Approximate pin.

places.w: A family fall farm in Columbiana built for a day with kids: a hayride out to a 10-acre pick-your-own pumpkin patch, a straw maze and a 4-acre corn maze, plus a petting zoo and a tractor-tire playground.
places.k: Seasonal (fall), about $7 admission. ~30 min south. Approximate pin.

places.ad: 3115 E Western Reserve Rd, Poland, OH
places.w: A popular Poland fall farm close to the city — a hayride to the pumpkin patch and a corn maze, cheap and cheerful.
places.k: Seasonal (fall), about $5 per person. ~15 min out. Approximate pin.
